exposure: ethnic origin (Europeans, Asians, Latin Americans, and Africans)
cohort: 3556 singleton pregnant women (≥ 24 weeks of gestation) who delivered during a 3-year period in an Italian free care hospital (1092 immigrants and 2464 Italians)
finding: Immigrant women experienced higher rates of macrosomia, very low birth weight, very early preterm delivery, and gestational diabetes mellitus compared to Italian women, while Italian women had a higher overall cesarean section rate.
mod_finding: The overall rate of cesarean sections was higher among Italian mothers compared to immigrants.
